title: Shorts crushing it (PF 1.84, 55% WR), Longs bleeding (PF 0.58, 37% WR) in live crypto perps. Directional centroids or macro regime gate?
author: Trader_for_earner
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I've been live paper-trading / micro-sizing a multi-pair systematic crypto perp trading system across 10 liquid altcoins (APT, SEI, ADA, OP, PENDLE, ARB, etc.) using automated WebSocket execution, strict ATR-based bracket SL/TP, and regime-based clustering.

Over our latest sample of 28 consecutive live executions across multiple intraday setups (VWAP\_DEVIATION, VWAP\_PULLBACK, BREAKOUT\_RETEST, TREND\_PULLBACK), we noticed a stark directional divergence and wanted to get the community's quantitative perspective.

\### 📊 Performance Breakdown:

| Metric | Overall | SHORT (SELL) | LONG (BUY) |

|:---|:---|:---|:---|

| \*\*Total Trades\*\* | 28 | 20 (71.4%) | 8 (28.6%) |

| \*\*Win Rate\*\* | 50.0% | \*\*55.0%\*\* (11W / 9L) | \*\*37.5%\*\* (3W / 5L) |

| \*\*Profit Factor (PF)\*\* | 1.45 | \*\*1.84\*\* | \*\*0.58\*\* |

| \*\*Payoff Ratio\*\* | 1.45 | \*\*1.51\*\* | \*\*0.97\*\* |

| \*\*Net P&L\*\* | +$0.6312 | \*\*+$0.8870\*\* | \*\*-$0.2558\*\* |

| \*\*Exit Types\*\* | 9 TP, 11 SL, 8 TTL | 8 TP, 7 SL, 5 TTL | 1 TP, 4 SL, 3 TTL |

\*(Note: Position sizing is kept strictly equalized per trade at \~$0.15–$0.20 risk per bet. TTL = Hard chronological time stop exit).\*

\---

\### 🔍 Observations:

1. \*\*Opportunity Skew:\*\* The scan engine triggered 2.5x more short setups than long setups (20 vs 8), reflecting the broader higher-timeframe (1h/4h) bearish / distribution drift across altcoins over this window.

2. \*\*Follow-Through Discrepancy:\*\*

   \- \*\*Shorts:\*\* Breakdowns and pullback continuations followed through cleanly to the full Take-Profit target (8 explicit TP fills). Volatility expansion worked in favor of the trade.

   \- \*\*Longs:\*\* Only \*\*1 out of 8 longs hit full Take-Profit\*\*. The other 2 "wins" barely survived into slight green before being closed out by the systematic Hard Time Stop. Longs suffered heavily from liquidity wicks and lacked sustained momentum.

3. \*\*Setup Performance:\*\*

   \- \`VWAP\_DEVIATION\` (Scalper): Performed well on both sides (67% WR on Longs, 80% WR on Shorts, total net profitable).

   \- \`VWAP\_PULLBACK\`: 50% WR on Shorts vs 25% WR on Longs. Longs suffered from "catching falling knives".

   \- \`BREAKOUT\_RETEST\`: 75% WR on Shorts vs 0% WR on Longs (classic bull trap failures in a weak macro regime).

\---

\### ❓ Questions for Quants & Systematic Traders:

1. \*\*Parameter Segregation by Side:\*\* Do you optimize separate parameter sets / centroids (e.g., separate ATR multipliers for SL/TP, trailing triggers) for Longs vs Shorts? Or does this risk overfitting to recent regime drift?

2. \*\*Long Target Compression:\*\* Given that crypto sell-offs are violent and expansions rapid, while rallies in choppy regimes are grindy and wick-heavy, do you use tighter TP multiples or faster trailing stops on Longs compared to Shorts?

3. \*\*HTF Regime Gating vs Symmetrical Trading:\*\* Do you completely suppress long pullback/breakout trades when the HTF (e.g. 4h/1d) is trading below key moving averages / negative drift, or do you simply raise the confidence threshold required to take the trade?

4. \*\*Sample Size Consideration:\*\* With N = 28 trades (N = 8 on Longs), how much weight would you place on this asymmetry right now versus waiting for N = 50 or N = 100?

Would love to hear how experienced algo traders handle directional asymmetry and regime alignment in crypto perps!
